04/06/2017
What are you not
 
	I’m a little teapot short and stout. I’m also not very honest. Note here that I have avoided the Epimenides paradox by not claiming that I always lie. Everybody lies, as much as everybody dies. I think that the ninth commandment was poorly thought out, like rules parents make for their first child- well meant, but without any thought to realism. Either that or God really didn’t want real estate prices in heaven going up. Being priced out of heaven by humans would be too much of a hilarious straight shooting comedy for Jesus after all.
	But even in this sad cesspool of sin, something my Catholic school assured me the earth is, I’m particularly bad at observing this particular commandment. Lying comes a little too naturally to me. I’m not sure why. If I had to guess though, I would say that I’m afraid. In fact, I think the main, or perhaps only reason people lie is because they’re afraid. Afraid of rejection, of being found out for the fraud that they think they are, afraid of reality. So according to transitive properties I must lie more than everyone else because I’m more afraid than everyone else.
	Now that took a rather dark turn. But hey, I could be lying. Because what could I possibly be so afraid of? Why should I be more afraid than everyone else? It seems rather presumptuous to say that I’m more afraid. After all the mortality rate of my peer group should be orders of magnitude lower than that of people in Israel, or the middle-eastern countries seemingly constantly at war against … democracy(?), I think is what the media tells me. My mortality rate is so low that I know stupid facts like that eating one-thousand bananas will increase my mortality rate by 1 micromort, meaning that the probability of my death goes up by one millionth. This is rather impressive. I will soon look into buying one thousand bananas. These challenges are really what makes me feel alive. Thrilling.
	Maybe I’m afraid of being dropped, of people finding out that I’m some sort of failure and deciding that I’m not worth their time. So perhaps I’m not very confident. This seems to feel like it has some inkling of truth. Like many deep seated traumas, this one could even be rooted in my childhood. Those moments when I returned home with a bad grade and had to then endure hours of being shouted at, or saying that I wanted to be an artist and having my drawings be mocked. At the very least, modern outlooks on parenting trends seem to agree with me. Look at that, by asking what I’m not, I have seem to started to answer what I am. Well, let’s not dwell in this place too much. The pained confusion of why I’m not confident is much more enjoyable to read than me moaning about why I am unconfident; a rather drab and common topic on internet forums.
	I’m not honest, but I try my best to be genuine. Oddly, I have come to realize more and more that those who live life to the fullest seem to make a habit of being honest. So I don’t think I can live a genuine life without living an honest life. Being afraid of reality and rejection would mean that I can only run and stuff my head in the sand- an idiom that has its roots in ostrich behavior by the way. 
	But I’m pretty sure I’m not an ostrich.
I think I like this answer to this prompt.
I am not an ostrich.

04/14/2017
What happened on that Day?

	It was daytime. It was a warm daytime with sunlight streaming in through glass doors that led out to the balcony and a brilliant Californian day. The fan beat overhead, almost silent, attempting to chase the heat away. I held a heavy book in my hands. It dealt with patricide and Russia, with faith and cynicism, jealousy and honor; my world. It was the world that I had always tried to understand a little more of using the conflicting nature of people shown to us through ageless classics.
	But it was such a nice day outside. I had long forgotten how nice a warm day feels, what it was like to smile only because the sky was blue. The catalyst for this change was a few feet away tapping away at a keyboard, frowning at some probability problem that had to do with efficiently finding the maximum using some kind of random walk. Interesting, terribly complicated, and, according to her, a very fun problem to think about.
	My mind drifted from the book to a conversation we had had yesterday. I wanted things to change, and I wanted somehow to change them. She replied that I was obviously miserable, that I was missing the entire point of being alive. I retorted with a bible parable, her with a story about seagulls. ‘I want to help’ was my stance. ‘But you aren’t free’ was her reply. Maybe that’s why I like reading Dostoevsky, I thought, because his characters seemed caged, angry.
I shifted on the couch, curling into a more comfortable position. The sun sinking into evening… tempting me to close my eyes. My mind was hopelessly scattered now. We had talked about empathy and sympathy. To understand one person IS to sympathize with them! Was her declaration against my point that these were different. I explained that to understand doesn’t mean that you sympathize, because sympathy seems to imply some form of compassion. Yet we can hate ourselves, showing that even in extreme instances of empathy there can be a plausible absence of sympathy. Yes, okay, but why do you care? Because I want to know how we can properly sympathize with each other.  But why?! Because then no one would have to feel hopelessly isolated. Again her signature frown- she was thinking about it. It interested her. A compliment.

My mind kept wandering, always into the same person.

She was the most straightforward person that I had ever met.

It’s so easy to be healthy! You just have to know that you want it and then just do it! Was her take on exercise. ‘But what if I feel lazy?’ I ventured. Then you ARE lazy. It was a merciless response, but fair enough. I started jogging. There was also a laughably convoluted conversation about how cutting carbs would free me from being dictated by hunger, and enable me to pursue what trains of thought I’d want. So of course, I started eating salads. 

I wanted to know what living this straightforward life was like.

	I had been closing a chapter in my life. One written by wanting to be myself in a world that seemed perversely interested in finding ways to kick me down. Such a life, I realized, was defined by staying standing despite everything crushing you, which meant being defined by resilience and a lurking anger. When everything belittles you, anger can keep you up. Anger, idealism, or indifference. But I wasn’t being attacked any more. All my coping mechanisms were doing nothing, all my walls and mirrors protecting me from threats now only imagined, hemming me in. I felt empty, hopelessly weighed down by all these self-made structures that no one could understand. The driving force of anger had burned to nothing, leaving me cold. Why was I here? Who was to blame? I hated it all.
	Well if you don’t like it so much you don’t have to be alive you know! Just get a knife or something and ask if you really want to live, and you do, of course you do! Because you’re alive right?! A challenge that hung in the air, her outburst a little too passionate for the talk we were having. I gave an awkward smile, remembering. A knife, me. No cuts, no dramatic gestures, no plea for attention. Just me, a knife, and a question. The question. I had felt tired, so tired. I said so, her expression softened. We were both talking from experience.
 	We’re here because we want to be. She started. So stop being so damn miserable? I finished. She smiled. Yes. Exactly.

“Arrrgh.”
A frustrated grumble took me out of my dozy memories. I looked over at the small hunched figure with her head in her hands.
“Having trouble?”
“Yes, I’m sure I can figure it out. I just need time to... How’s your book?”
“Interesting, just read a chapter called ‘The Inquisitor’. It’s about how… well… it’s complicated.”
“Tell me.”
I ambled over to the table, collecting my thoughts. Long shadows sprawled across the living room floor, the sun flaring orange for the final hour before it set. She was here for a few more days, then we’ll never see each other again. That was fine. I would miss her, but that was fine as well. We would trade presents, and say our goodbyes, and that was how life flowed by, how people passed by. But today I looked out at a beautiful day and appreciated the sun’s warmth, looked up into a clear sky and smiled at its clarity. It had been a fine day.

Why bother?

	Ah, hello old friend. I hope it’s fair to call a question a friend, since friendship is really only a matter of intimacy. I wonder if there has been a single day in the past decade where you have not taken up at least some corner of my thoughts. Such an incessant friend, so needy, and unrelenting. We’ve been down many paths trying to satiate your need to be answered, your need to be truly understood and satisfied. As is the case with old friends, I feel that I’ve perhaps adopted too many of your mannerisms and your mode of thinking. I’ve spent entire days pondering what you mean. I’ve even let you creep into conversations with my other friends, and the need for an answer grows only stronger with every failure.
	I first really made an acquaintance in the very early years. You make yourself known best when there is something making me do things I do not want to: when there are tests I don’t care about, when I have to perform actions I have no real investment in, and when I find effort to be just too much at certain points in time. So I would get to know you through the times when I was in my room, trying to live the dreams of other people, making myself act stronger than I felt.
	As I grew older I’ve found that you have a lot of friends, lots of people you bothered with your presence. One frenchman even said “There is only one really serious philosophical question, and that is suicide.” Boy you really drove that man up the wall. Remember that time when I thought that life was about what you can leave behind? About the people who will pick up your dreams and keep whatever fire you lit burning towards the ends of eternity? I really did read too much fantasy back in the day. There was also a short stint where I thought life was about being nice to other people and trying to understand them. That was really the bible talking, but it really helped me question morality in interesting ways later down the line. So I guess I salvaged something out of that mess. I had a stage where I thought life was about hope, and about breaking apart everything to grab only whatever happiness I could. I think I was sad then, and your constant questioning of my life choices made me selfish and very angry. It didn’t help that around about this time we thought that life might be about trying to help the people we care about. Figuring out that those same people can hurt you in ways we thought I was already guarded against wasn’t much fun, especially when it happened a few more times. Well, fool me twice I guess.

Myself and the world

The idea exists to be expressed. The thought is the why and what of what we do.

It's an odd way to start off a concept, but I mean that the existence of ideas means the existence of the person. The person is defined by what they think and why they think it. Negatives, positives, empathy, cruelty, faith, disbelief; they're all rooted in thought.

As an extension of this thought, it would be fair to think that the idea is the world. The world is defined by what we think regardless of how the world itself is arranged. The world is indifferent, we just shape it to be cruel or kind. Mind over matter.

The thought leads onto the very basic concept that everyone lives in their own world, completely different from the world of others. Every mind is a world for the world is in the eyes of the beholder.

Doesn't this worry you sometimes? What if that one person you thought was nice to you actually just thought nothing of you? What if those who you thought were significant in your life held you in no significance at all?
Also, on brighter notes, what if people you just passed by everyday perceived so much more beauty in the everyday than you ever did. It could very well be that the stony faced person whom you ridiculed for being one of the herd actually ponders questions that would befuddle you even with the very basic openings of its argument.

The world is acting on you, but at the same time you are acting on the world. You cannot simply be a victim to any whim of fate. A victim of fate is one who resolutely chooses to fall, not one who accepts the fall.
The fall itself is avoidable, but will most probably come with a life of mere existence.

The master of the world is you. To complain has no meaning in such a world. To believe is to make possible. To act is everything. Boldness is magic.

Myself and you

And hello stranger! Here is myself, and there is yourself. Who am I? And who are you? I would much like to tell you who I am, and I would much like to hear who you are.

But how limited our means to do this. All language and art can't cover our whole existence. For my thoughts create a world, and your thoughts your world.
How can we express a world of thoughts with words so untrained? Or with drawings so unpolished? Even with mastery, perhaps I would be able to show you just one instant of thought that I hold precious. If I ever do I only hope that you too will hold this moment precious.

To say that a world exists in one's mind sounds marvelous! Doesn't it quite? To say that 'I'm special because I hold my own world'. But how sad is it at the same time to hold a whole world to yourself. Is it not depressing to think that I live in such isolation from you, and you from me? I'm afraid that my world is rather queer and alien. I hope it does not dissuade you from knowing me.

For I want to be known. I do so very want to be seen. I do so very want to see. What lies past that smiling face that you always put on and what thoughts beyond the 'how are you's and 'I'm doing great thank you!'

Because without this the world is a world of worlds. And in so many worlds one little thought does get rather lonely. Are you not lonely too? So unsure and ill-placed?
